abstract: We prove short product moments for actual Möbius character polynomials over the Eisenstein field, together with extended single-polynomial ranges and an explicit zero-density theorem. For natural rows of index norm at most $P$, a fixed product of $k$ centrally normalized inverse polynomials, with total length $Y$, has squared mean bounded by $(PYNE)^\epsilon T^J(P+P^{1/3}Y)$. Here $E$ is a common deletion, $T$ bounds the common norm heights, and the fixed finite character is principal. In particular, the inverse fourth moment has a diagonal-size upper bound through length $P^{1/3}$; the corresponding $2k$-th moment range is $L\leq P^{2/(3k)}$. The proof extends reverse Poisson and averaged Type I/II estimates to coefficients of fixed products of reciprocal Dirichlet series. It retains the character zero that keeps a Type II product row cube-free, averages the amplifier in the raw Gauss source, and restores all repeated primes and natural cube towers. A common Mellin integral preserves the separate smooth profiles. Coupling the inverse fourth moment to an ordinary fourth moment gives the mixed bound $P+P^{2/3}R$ for an inverse product of total length $R$ and one full ordinary factor, on nonprincipal rows. For one polynomial, the untwisted unnormalized bound is $PY+P^{1/3}Y^2$. Combined with the previous long-range argument, it gives power savings for $P^{1/2+\gamma}\leq Y\leq P^{2-\tau}$, with fixed positive buffers and small moving data. A seven-factor Gram comparison gives lower exponent $12/17$ for an arbitrary fixed finite Hecke character. We retain the density exponent $E_4(7/8)=9/22$. Exact algebra checks accompany the analytic proofs. The current signed-remainder threshold is matched but not surpassed. No new individual zero-free region or resolution of the Riemann hypothesis follows.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Extend the actual Möbius mean to lower length exponent 12/17 for a general fixed finite character, and prove the principal-character bound PY+P^(1/3)Y² for P>=Y. The latter uses raw Type I source averaging, a retained zero in the cube-free Type II rows, all cube towers and reverse Poisson. Together with the previous near-P argument it gives principal lower exponent 1/2. Section 3.9 extends the proof to fixed shifted reciprocal products, retaining every powerful factor and the separate original profiles. Section 3.10 gives the normalized inverse-product mean P+P^(1/3)Y on natural rows for all relative lengths. It yields inverse 2k-th moments of diagonal size through L=P^(2/(3k)), including an inverse fourth moment through P^(1/3). Combining it with the ordinary fourth moment gives P+P^(2/3)R for an inverse product of total length R and one full ordinary factor on nonprincipal rows, in fixed polynomial length ranges. Add exact coefficient checks, source details and scope comparisons. The density exponents are unchanged. No improved complete signed remainder, individual zero-free region or RH claim is made.
title: Short Möbius product moments and explicit zero density for cubic Hecke characters
